Proposition
[smoothness criterion in the conformal polar-coordinate model]

Source: petersen:page-0155 ↗ def:pet-ch4-warped-product-conformal-forms For $dr^2+\varphi ^2(r)ds_{n-1}^2=\psi ^2(\rho )\big(d\rho ^2+\rho ^2ds_{n-1}^2\big)$ with $\varphi (r_0)=0$, $\rho (r_0)=0$ at $r_0\in \partial I$: the right-hand side is smooth at $\rho =0$ iff $\psi (0)>0$ and $\psi ^{(\mathrm{odd})}(0)=0$; translated back to $\varphi $, this is the usual criterion $\dot\varphi (r_0)=\pm 1$, $\varphi ^{(\mathrm{even})}(r_0)=0$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch4-conformal-smoothness-criterion \sketch A radial conformal factor extends smoothly across the Euclidean origin exactly when it is the restriction of a smooth even function of $\rho $, with positive value there. This is equivalent to $\psi (0)>0$ and the vanishing of all odd derivatives. Translating Taylor series through either radial substitution in subsection 3.3 gives $\dot\varphi (r_0)=\pm 1$ and vanishing even derivatives of $\varphi $.

□
